newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends steady on Central Bank move.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends steady on Central Bank move.

text.p: * Central Bank seen net buyer of dollars
The Philippine peso ended unchanged on Monday at 26.28 pesos as the Central Bank sold dollars at that rate to limit the peso's decline, traders said.
Overall, however, the Central Bank was seen to be a net buyer of dollars, with purchases of about $28 million and sales of $8.5 million, one dealer estimated.
The peso started strong but weakened after the Central Bank raised its bid rate for the dollar to 26.275 from 26.268/269.

"The Central Bank was buying dollars to recover the dollars it sold last Friday," one dealer said. According to the Central Bank, it was a net seller of dollars on Friday in the amount of $56.50 million.
In general, banks favoured buying the dollar because of the narrower interest premium of the peso over the dollar, dealers said.
Another trader said the view is that monetary authorities would let the peso to slowly depreciate to help stave off a wider trade deficit.
Dealers pointed out the Central Bank had set the trend for a slow depreciation of the peso for the past month.
Traders also believe there was dollar demand from foreign funds exiting from the country's stock market.
A $28-million requirement of oil companies also gave some push for the dollar but these were easily satisfied at 26.278 pesos, dealers said.
The day's average yielded 26.278 pesos to the dollar from 26.276, with turnover thinning to $95.50 million from $206.60 million.
